script:
Presenter: Why was this project started?
Khalid: We wanted to make heritage walking route because our school community needed a practical improvement.
Presenter: Where did you plan the first version?
Khalid: We began in the old souq, where our teacher organised responsibilities for everyone.
Presenter: When was the team meeting held?
Khalid: It was Saturday morning, which allowed our team to prepare without missing lessons.
Presenter: Which item was particularly useful?
Khalid: We used a printed map, and checked that it was suitable for the task.
Presenter: Who checked the details and safety?
Khalid: We consulted a local guide instead of trusting rumours or making unsupported claims.
Presenter: Did students work completely alone?
Khalid: No, our teacher supervised carefully, while students researched information and shared different responsibilities.
Presenter: What problem appeared during the project?
Khalid: Our first attempt contained a wrong street name, so the results needed further checking.
Presenter: How did your group correct the error?
Khalid: We returned to the road sign and explained our correction clearly to teammates.
Presenter: Who will benefit from your work?
Khalid: We hope visiting families will gain useful information from the finished project.
Presenter: What did users suggest improving?
Khalid: They recommended more rest stops, and we recorded their suggestions for the next version.
Presenter: How did you handle disagreements?
Khalid: We listened respectfully, considered the evidence and tested the strongest suggestions together.
Presenter: What did the team do with feedback?
Khalid: We discussed comments at our weekly meeting and made a clear improvement plan.
Presenter: What will you prepare next term?
Khalid: Our next step will be a library exhibition, building on the experience gained this term.
Presenter: What is the most important lesson?
Khalid: We learned the value of respectful tourism, honest feedback and careful preparation. Every group member also checked the final explanation and asked useful questions before sharing it with others.
